name: Bonaventure Cemetery
unique: A Victorian cemetery on a bluff over the Wilmington River, with live oaks, Spanish moss and the graves that made Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil famous.
buzz: People come for the book and stay for the sculpture. Go early, keep your voice down, and skip it during a funeral.

name: Tybee Island
unique: Savannah's beach town, with a working lighthouse you can climb, wide sand, a pier and loggerhead turtles nesting on the dunes in summer.
buzz: Parking is the main cost and the main hassle. North Beach is quieter, and the turtle patrol runs night walks in season.

name: The Grey
unique: A restored 1938 Art Deco Greyhound bus station turned restaurant, with a curved counter, leather booths and a menu that reads the Lowcountry through a Black Southern lens.
buzz: Book weeks out and sit at the counter if you can. People talk about the service as much as the food, and the room is the occasion.

name: American Prohibition Museum
customer: Families with teens, history people, couples
unique: A museum of the dry years with costumed guides, a speakeasy at the end and a replica still, in a city that never really stopped drinking.
buzz: More fun than a history museum has a right to be, and the speakeasy cocktail is included in some tickets. The tour is the way to do it.

name: Hay House
unique: A seven level Italianate mansion with a cantilevered spiral staircase, hand painted ceilings and the first indoor plumbing of its kind in the state.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and the guides know the family scandals. The behind the scenes tour on select Saturdays is worth the upgrade.

name: Cox Capitol Theatre
unique: A 1916 vaudeville house turned rock room, with a balcony, a painted ceiling and a schedule that runs from indie acts to comedy nights.
buzz: The room is the draw, small enough that every seat feels close. Check the calendar rather than dropping in.

name: International Cherry Blossom Festival
unique: Ten days of pink in a city that claims 300,000 cherry trees, with a parade, concerts, a bed race and pancakes at the Kiwanis tent.
buzz: The trees are the excuse and the civic energy is the point. Parking downtown is easier than expected on weekdays.

name: Tubman Museum
unique: One of the largest museums of African American art and history in the South, with a gallery of Black artists and an exhibit on the Middle Georgia civil rights movement.
buzz: The art collection is stronger than visitors expect and the local history is told plainly. Allow two hours.

name: National Infantry Museum
unique: A 190,000 square foot museum with a soldier art gallery, a Vietnam helicopter, a World War II street and a basic training simulator, on the edge of Fort Benning.
buzz: People plan an hour and stay four. The Last 100 Yards gallery is the emotional center, and admission is free.

name: Chattahoochee Riverwalk
unique: A 15 mile paved trail along the Chattahoochee, with river access, bridges and a skyline that mixes mills and whitewater.
buzz: Flat, shaded in stretches and busy at dusk. Rent a bike or walk to the whitewater course and watch the rafts.

name: Columbus Museum
unique: A free museum with American art, decorative arts and a hands on history gallery about the Chattahoochee valley, plus a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and quietly good, with a strong regional collection. The children's gallery is a real one, not a corner of toys.

name: Oxbow Meadows Environmental Learning Center
unique: A nature center on a bend of the Chattahoochee with live reptiles, a pollinator garden and trails through bottomland forest, run by the university.
buzz: Cheap, hands on and good with kids. The snake room is the highlight and the trails are flat.

name: Radium Springs Gardens
unique: Georgia's largest natural spring, pumping 70,000 gallons a minute into a blue pool, the surviving centerpiece of a 1920s resort that once drew celebrities.
buzz: The water is astonishingly blue and the ruins of the resort give it a melancholy. Free, flat and easy, with turtles on the logs.

name: Chehaw Park and Zoo
unique: A zoo and 700 acre park with a splash pad, a nature trail, a train and a collection heavy on African and North American animals.
buzz: Good value for a family day, with enough shade to survive a Georgia summer. The train is the kid favorite.

name: Albany Civil Rights Institute
unique: A museum in the old Mount Zion Baptist Church, where the Albany Movement was organized, with the pews, the jail cell and the freedom songs still attached to the room.
buzz: The church itself is the exhibit and the oral histories are powerful. Ask about the SNCC volunteers and the mass meetings.

name: Flint RiverQuarium
unique: An aquarium built around a 175,000 gallon blue hole fed by the Flint River, with otters, alligators and a walk through the spring.
buzz: Small enough for young kids and unusual because the water is real river water. The outdoor aviary is a bonus.
